analyzed_vuln.description: The bug is a partially-initialized attribute argument zval being left in `attr->argv[]` when attribute argument compilation/evaluation fails on malformed input (`s->getAtelf::FOO` in the PoC). In `zend_compile_attributes()`, `zend_add_attribute()` allocates the attribute and sets `argc`, but `attr->argv[j]` entries are not pre-initialized to `UNDEF` before `zend_const_expr_to_zval()` fills them. If that conversion aborts early for one argument, later shutdown frees the attribute via `free_attribute()` in `zend_attributes.c`, which blindly runs `zval_ptr_dtor(&attr->argv[i])` for all `i < argc`, causing destructor/GC on garbage zvals and crashing in `zend_gc_delref`.
analyzed_vuln.conditions: Trigger requires parsing code that creates attributes with argument expressions where at least one argument fails constant-expression conversion after the attribute object has already been allocated with nonzero argc. Data flow: fuzzer input -> parser/compiler -> `zend_compile_attributes()` allocates attribute (`zend_add_attribute`) and starts populating argv -> malformed attribute arg causes premature failure, leaving some argv slots uninitialized -> request shutdown destroys op_array attributes (`destroy_op_array` -> hash destroy -> `free_attribute`) -> invalid `zval_ptr_dtor` on uninitialized argv element leads to wild read/SEGV in `zend_gc_delref`.
